extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, comedy writers, and humor enthusiasts (fans/analysts of comedic technique)
extracted.subtask_description: Analyze and/or adopt Norm Macdonald's deadpan, rambling comedic method—how to wander conversationally around a core punchline, build tension, and use long-form shaggy-dog storytelling. The guidance is aimed at performers and writers wanting to understand why this style lands and how to execute it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadpan delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm’s deadpan, rambling style is the perfect delivery mechanism for his observations about life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a low-affect, seemingly unaffected tone so absurdities land against a flat presentation. Deadpan pairs with rambling to create the comic contrast; avoid overtly emoting the punchline. Example: Norm's Netflix special and interviews show laughter generated by subdued delivery rather than high-energy performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meandering/rambling around a core punchline
rubrics_metrics.description: “I think of a great, great punchline and then I just wander around... You just think of little jokes knowing the giant joke is coming… I’m just circling it like the satellite the moon is circling this whirling cinder we call earth.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from a central joke idea and wander conversationally: add small asides, tangents, and side jokes while continually returning toward the main payoff. This technique helps avoid rote repetition and keeps material feeling fresh. Avoid aimless tangents that never relate back to the core punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvisation to keep material fresh
rubrics_metrics.description: Improv-inspired rambling solves the problem of repeating the same jokes over and over every night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate spontaneous-sounding improvisations and variations around set material so that repeated performances feel new. This is a practical strategy for touring comics who can't realistically perform an identical scripted routine every show. Careful balance is needed: improvisation should enhance, not obscure, the main joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shaggy dog story / long-buildup format
rubrics_metrics.description: The shaggy dog story is a type of joke that depends upon a long buildup that contentedly holds off the anticlimactic punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use extended, detail-rich storytelling that appears to be going nowhere to build audience tension and anticipation; the eventual anticlimactic payoff provides release. Best for performers comfortable with long-form storytelling and who can maintain interest with colorful asides. The post warns this format can be crude/NSFW depending on content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating tension by delayed payoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustained notes (pedal points) create tension. The longer the better. The audience is wondering: when is this thing going to end?!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay the punchline deliberately to increase audience curiosity and tension. Use pacing and sustained focus on peripheral details to make listeners lean in. Risk: overextension can lose the room if the performer doesn't maintain intrigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pepper narrative with seemingly irrelevant details
rubrics_metrics.description: Shaggy dog and rambling styles pepper the narrative with seemingly irrelevant details to support the drift and delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include apparently extraneous particulars that enrich texture and distract from the inevitable payoff; they help disguise the setup and maintain rhythm. However, details should still be entertaining or evocative—avoid filler that bores the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek comedic potential in mundane topics
rubrics_metrics.description: When someone brings up a topic, the mind flashes 'Stick with this! There’s something funny in here somewhere…' Examples: colonoscopies, divorces, drywall installation techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for humor in ordinary, everyday experiences. Confidence that a punchline exists lets you wander and build the joke organically. Avoid forcing novelty—start from honest curiosity about the topic's absurdities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk/edge through controversial subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm steers conversations into dangerous waters of controversial topics like gender identity politics, creating palpable tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using controversial or boundary-pushing topics can generate strong comedic payoff via discomfort and tension, but requires skillful handling to avoid alienating the audience. Be prepared for guests or listeners to feel uncomfortable; the technique depends on skilled navigation of those responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing the straight-man/double-comic dilemma
rubrics_metrics.description: The dilemma is always: who is going to be the straight man? Two comedians both trying to be funny at the same time can create tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performing with others, decide who will play the straight-man role or intentionally let both play against-type for comedic friction. In interviews, guests must be 'conversationally fit' to handle a rambling host—otherwise the dynamic becomes awkward. Use role awareness to control comedic flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performing an illusion of altered affect (e.g., 'drunk' persona)
rubrics_metrics.description: Merchant: 'You’re not even drunk. And yet, the illusion of it is extraordinary.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting an altered-affect persona (slightly off-kilter, weathered, or 'drunk') can enhance comedic unpredictability without actually being impaired. The performer should maintain underlying control so the 'illusion' reads as deliberate character work rather than sloppy delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic dominance via presence and conversational control
rubrics_metrics.description: It's clear that you need to be conversationally fit to sit across from Norm Macdonald for an hour... it's not always obvious that Norm requires your presence to conduct a compelling interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop stage presence and the ability to sustain long-form monologue so you can carry an extended bit and keep listeners engaged even when others are minimally contributing. In shared formats (interviews/panels), the performer can still command humor by steering topics and timing.
